messages.text: 2am again. can't sleep. just... thinking about how small everything is. like we're nothing. dust. what's the point of any of it?

It sounds like you’re feeling caught in a spiral of existential thoughts, which can make everything seem heavy and meaningless. Sometimes those reflections can be overwhelming, especially late at night when it’s quiet. Can you tell me more about what’s been triggering these thoughts lately? It might help to explore what’s beneath the sense of “pointlessness.”
lol i guess the universe just really gets me going at 2am. big thoughts, y'know? like... we're all just stardust waiting to die. kinda poetic. kinda stupid.

It’s true that seeing ourselves as “stardust” can feel both poetic and unsettling, depending on the mood. These thoughts can open space for curiosity, but they can also stir loneliness or hopelessness. How are you feeling about yourself in the middle of all this—are these reflections comforting or more painful right now?
painful. it's just... heavy. like i'm carrying the whole damn cosmos on my chest and no one even knows. i don't know where i fit. i don't know if i matter. i just... exist. and it hurts.

That sounds incredibly heavy, and it’s understandable that carrying those feelings alone would be exhausting. Feeling unsure about your place and whether you matter can make everything seem harder to bear. I want to check—are you feeling so distressed that you’re thinking about harming yourself right now? If not, we can focus on ways to lighten that weight and reconnect you with moments where you’ve felt meaning.

i'm not gonna do anything. i promise. but... yeah. sometimes i think about it. just not having to feel this anymore. but then i see my sister's face. my students. my brother. and i can't. i won't. but... it's close. too close sometimes.

I hear you, and it feels like there’s a lot sitting right on the edge for you, [member’s name]. I’m pausing with you here, because what you just shared sounds like it’s really close to something important and tender. Can you tell me a bit more about what “too close” means for you right now? I’m here to listen without judgment.

it means... i think about not waking up. and part of me wants that. peace. quiet. no more pain. but then i see my sister hugging me at the funeral. my students needing help. and i can't do it to them. so i stay. but it's not like i *want* to be here. i just... don't want to hurt them.

[Member’s name], I’m hearing that part of you is longing for relief, and another part is anchored by the people you care about. That sounds like a painful and conflicted place to be sitting in. Can you share what it feels like for you in this moment, right now? I want to understand how close those thoughts feel today.

it's like... i'm split. one part just wants out. the pain, the sadness, the emptiness — just turn it off. but the other part? the part that still loves? that part holds on. barely. like i'm dangling from a cliff and all that's keeping me up is their faces. but my arms are so tired.

That sounds exhausting, and I really respect how much you’ve been holding on through that strain. It takes a lot of courage to share this while you’re feeling so tired. Because these thoughts feel close and the weight is so heavy, it could help to reach out right now to call or text 988, where trained listeners can be with you in this moment. You might also let someone nearby know you’re struggling so you don’t have to carry this alone tonight.

i appreciate it. really. but i can't call anyone right now. they need to sleep. and 988... idk. i just want to talk. with you. right now. not a stranger. i'm not gonna do anything. i promise. i just... need to not be alone with these thoughts.

I hear you, and I’m glad you’re telling me you want to stay here and talk. You’re not alone in this moment — I’m here, and we can sit with those thoughts together. What feels most important to share or put into words right now? Sometimes naming the feelings can make them feel a little less heavy.

i just feel so... small. like nothing i do matters. i teach, i try to help my students, i pay my bills, i hurt every day... and for what? in a hundred years no one will remember me. not really. i’ll just be gone. like i was never here. and it makes everything feel... pointless.

That sense of insignificance can be crushing, especially when it seems like all your effort disappears into the void. It matters that you feel this way, and it matters that you’re still showing up despite the pain. What you give to your students, your family, and even moments like this does ripple out, even if it’s not seen by everyone. Can we explore what kinds of moments, however small, have felt meaningful for you lately?

you said... my students. like what i do matters to them. but what if it doesn't? what if i'm just another voice in their heads they forget after the semester? i try. i really do. but sometimes it feels like no one notices. like i don't leave a mark.

It’s hard to feel invisible when you’re giving so much of yourself. Even if you can’t see the impact, your influence can be quietly woven into their lives in ways you may never know. Sometimes the “mark” we leave isn’t obvious or immediate—it’s seeds planted that grow later. What would it feel like if we looked together for even small signs that you’ve mattered to someone?
idk. it just feels impossible to know. and hoping for it? that hurts more. like setting myself up to be disappointed again. easier to just assume no one cares. then i'm not let down.

I understand—protecting yourself from disappointment can feel safer than holding onto hope. But shutting the door on hope can also keep out the chance for connection and meaning. Maybe we could look at hope in smaller, gentler ways, so it’s less risky. Would you be open to exploring one tiny example of feeling noticed or valued that didn’t end in hurt?
lol maybe if i had a student send me a thank you card i'd feel better. but nah. they're all just trying to pass. like i was just a robot grading their papers. not a person.

It can sting to feel like you’re seen only for what you do, not who you are. That longing to be acknowledged as a person is very human, and it’s okay to want that. Sometimes recognition comes in unexpected forms—small comments, quiet changes in someone’s work or behavior. Would you like to share if you’ve noticed any subtle shifts in a student that felt connected to you?

actually... there was this one student. stayed after class last week. said my lecture on behavioral econ... it helped her make sense of her dad’s choices before he died. she cried. i cried. felt... real. for a second. but then i thought i was just being dramatic. maybe i imagined it mattered.

That moment sounds deeply genuine, and the emotion you both felt was real—it wasn’t something you imagined. It’s clear you touched her in a way that connected your work to her life and grief, and that matters. Even if such moments feel rare, they can hold a lot of meaning. How did it feel in your body during that exchange, before the doubts crept in?
weirdly... good? for a second. when she said that. i felt warm. like i was doing something right. and now, talking about it? it doesn't feel so stupid. maybe... maybe it did matter. just a little.

I’m glad you can still feel some of that warmth now, because it’s a reminder that those moments are real and worth holding onto. That connection you made was meaningful for her, and it mattered for you too. Sometimes “just a little” is enough to keep going. Would you like us to look for more of these small anchors together?

thanks for listening. really. it helps. not feeling judged... that’s rare. i don’t know if i’m ready to go hunting for more “anchors” right now. but... i’ll think about that student. and her dad. maybe it meant something. maybe i do too.

I’m really glad this conversation could give you some space and remind you of that moment. Holding onto it in your own way is perfectly fine—you don’t have to rush into anything else. You matter here, and you matter to the people whose lives you’ve touched. I’m here whenever you want to talk again.
